comments: Candidate fixes leakage by filtering payments on ts, reviews on review_creation_date, and replacing mutable order_status flags with dated delivered/carrier events (< seed_time), while retaining the same product-level aggregation families; dropping canceled_share is justified since mutable status is the leak source, and additions (trends, recency) preserve intent.

Candidate fixes the review leakage by filtering on review_answer_timestamp < seed_time (original only filtered orders by purchase ts), and also correctly gates payments by ts and delivery features by delivered_customer_date < seed_time, while retaining and extending the original sales/review feature families.

Candidate fixes the unfiltered reviews fallback (now empty when no review_creation_date) and adds delivery/payment timestamp guards while retaining all original feature families plus safe additions; only residual concern is the payments ts-filter being conditional on column presence.

Candidate removes the unfiltered-reviews fallback (now requires review_creation_date <= seed_time) and time-filters payments via ts when available, while retaining all original feature families and adding only past-only derived features; residual risk is that payments without a ts column remain unfiltered, though they are restricted to orders purchased before seed_time.

Candidate fixes the unfiltered payments leak by filtering on payments['ts'] <= seed_time and keeps reviews filtered by review_creation_date, while retaining all original feature families (only adding a 180-day window and avg_payment_value); slight uncertainty remains because correctness depends on the 'ts' column being a true availability timestamp.

Candidate masks delivery/approval timestamps to pre-seed events, derives is_delivered from actual delivery date instead of mutable order_status, and filters seller_agg via time-filtered order_items, while retaining all original feature families.

Candidate gates delivery/approval/carrier timestamps and reviews/payments by seed_time, filters order_items by ts (fixing the unfiltered seller_agg), and drops mutable order_status, retaining the same product-level feature families with only minor payment aggregates (max/min) removed.

Candidate correctly time-filters items, reviews, payments and nulls future delivery/approval dates, but still uses the mutable order_status (and derived is_delivered/delivered_ratio) without any as-of-seed_time check, leaving a clear temporal violation.

The candidate correctly filters reviews by review_creation_date <= seed_time (fixing the delayed-review leak) and keeps all original feature families, but it newly aggregates order_status at snapshot time without an availability timestamp, so mutable status (e.g., delivered/canceled set after seed_time) may introduce a new temporal violation.
Candidate adds availability-time filters for reviews (review_creation_date), payments (ts), and delivery (delivered date <= seed_time) while retaining all original feature families and aggregates.

Candidate fixes all leaks (reviews filtered by review_creation_date, delivery/carrier dates masked to <= seed_time, payments filtered by ts <= seed_time) while retaining all original feature families with only additive features.

Candidate adds seed_time filters on review_creation_date, delivery/approval timestamps, and payment ts, fixing the original leakage from unfiltered reviews and future delivery dates, while retaining all original feature families (sales, reviews, payments, delivery, status) with only additive window features; the delivered_rate from mutable order_status is a minor residual concern.

Candidate fixes the leaked unfiltered review merge by filtering on review_creation_date < seed_time, also filters orders/payments by their timestamps and gates delivery status on delivered date < seed_time, while retaining all original feature families and only adding new ones.

Candidate filters reviews by review_creation_date, payments by ts, masks future delivery dates (delay computed only for delivered-before-seed orders), keeps all original feature families and adds only past-safe features.

The previously unfiltered review and payment joins are now restricted to records with review_creation_date/ts <= seed, orders are filtered by purchase timestamp, and new delivery features mask deliveries after seed, while all original feature families are retained.

Candidate adds availability-time filters for reviews (review_creation_date), payments (ts), and delivery (delivered date <= seed_time) while retaining the identical product-level feature set and seller aggregates.

Candidate correctly filters reviews by review_creation_date and gates delivery delay on delivery before seed_time, but still uses mutable order_status (is_canceled/is_delivered_rate) and includes payments without filtering by the available pay_ts, so residual temporal risk remains.

Candidate fixes the clear leaks (reviews filtered by review_creation_date < seed_time, delivery days only for orders delivered before seed_time, items gated by ts < seed_time) while retaining all original feature families and adding new ones; payments lack an explicit availability timestamp but are joined only to orders purchased before seed_time, which is a minor residual uncertainty rather than a clear new violation.

Candidate fixes the clear leakage (reviews now filtered by review_creation_date <= seed_time, delivery features restricted to orders delivered before seed_time, items by ts) while retaining all original feature families and adding new ones; only minor concern is the 90-day review window keyed on item purchase ts rather than review date, which is not a clear violation.

Original leaked future reviews (unfiltered merge on order_id); candidate filters reviews by review_creation_date < seed_time, payments by ts < seed_time, and orders/delivery by timestamps < seed_time, while retaining and extending the same sales/review/order/payment feature families.
